chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn Amr from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'How should I place my hand on the graves of the Muslims?' So he pointed with his hand to the ground, placed it upon it, while he was facing the Qibla.

key_terms.أَبَانٍ: Aban ibn Tammam, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and physical posture for placing one's hand on a grave during visitation?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the physical etiquette of *ziyarah* by placing his hand on the ground while facing the Qibla, establishing a direct link between the visitor and the deceased. This gesture reflects the Shia tradition of treating graves as sacred spaces for spiritual connection rather than mere burial sites, emphasizing humility and reverence. The act of facing the Qibla during this interaction underscores the unity of the deceased with the broader Muslim community in their orientation towards God.
